capabilities.scope: Rigid articulated URDF/SRDF import, semantic names, meshes, and deterministic fingerprints.
No production MJCF parser. A pinned G1 companion-MJCF preset is data, not general MJCF support.

Canonical models and WorldPack carry unique named link-local sites. TaskPack and SensorIR resolve a site plus an optional site-local offset into their existing body-frame records, including composed orientation and COM translation, with no runtime lookup or site-specific Metal branch. General MJCF site parsing is still blocked on the MJCF importer.

Qualified Apple-Metal rigid, articulated, and rod solver path: fixed temporal microsteps, coupled nonlinear block sweeps, retained banded rod response for generalized and surface-contact rows, immediate integration, and transactional warm state. This does not qualify all rod mechanics or the residual-converged profile.
Private residual-converged NumiSolver profile is available for focused study; its current backend is transitional and not yet the qualified production path.
NumiSolver uses temporal small steps but does not claim the complete vendor-specific PhysX TGS contract.
Shared row, endpoint, cone, stable-key, and warm-start representation. Active scalar joint limits and contacts are coupled in NumiSolver; generic runtime widths beyond three rows remain incomplete.
Selected convex event-time paths exist; complete advance-to-impact, solve, and continue coverage is not qualified.
Distinct fingerprinted URDF, companion-MJCF, and RL Lab actuator contracts; no silent 25/35/50 N m mixing.

The native session owns a topology-derived command-delay ring, deterministic backlash play, motor-envelope and dry-friction decomposition, and an eight-channel actuator-state SensorIR view. Delay is quantized upward to whole control periods, reset is neutral, and rejected physics submissions restore the pre-step timeline. Motor-envelope and passive-friction evaluation still occur at the control boundary rather than being re-evaluated at every physics microstep.

Swift schedules bounded native submissions; Metal owns persistent simulator state, asynchronous tickets, and per-environment physical publication. Physics, TaskIR, SensorIR, and actuator delay/backlash now participate in the native transaction; whole-session atomic reset across tactile, presentation, global curriculum, and future recurrent policy state remains incomplete.

The historical standalone probe forest has been deleted. The build now exposes seven native subsystem checks plus the Swift integration owner, one subcommand-based benchmark binary, one product example, two Swift products, and four installed offline compilers. Fifty unowned diagnostic source files and every probe-named target were removed; Git history is the recovery path. Physics, rollout, memory, and long-soak benchmark profiles still need to join the retained benchmark binary.

A reset is applied to working state only. A later pair-capacity failure restores the exact previously committed q/v, scene bodies, manifold headers/points/counts, SensorIR output and metadata, retains the resident token, and permits a following submission. Generalized warm starts, rods, and convex caches use the same pre-reset checkpoint ordering in code but still need focused reset-failure evidence.

The generated runtime schema owns every reachable pipeline, feature group, Metal entry point, host member, and threadgroup contract. Compiled feature selection creates only the required groups, later upgrades are additive, and three mutable state arenas share one immutable device/library/queue/pipeline cache. Metal 4 command allocators, generated argument tables, residency sets, and the final barrier graph remain incomplete.

In-process Swift/MLX PPO consumes lifetime-scoped native shared Metal rollout slots without Swift array concatenation, a Swift-side stream copy, an MLX input copy, duplicate compact MetalWorldResult vectors, or a CPU payload scan. The integration owner advances beyond the three-slot ring and validates release, policy revision, checkpoints, and artifacts.

The native runtime owns three fixed-capacity shared Metal slots for actor and critic observations, latents, behavior metadata, values, bootstrap values, and transitions. Swift receives only opaque leases; managed MLX C arrays retain and release the slot payload deterministically.

The world command buffer blits every compact learning stream directly into the pending native rollout lease. The lease cursor advances only with accepted world publication; the owner checks two-chunk offsets, bootstrap placement, byte-exact content, premature visibility rejection, exclusivity, reuse, and a leased-only result with zero duplicate host learning elements.

One cooperative Metal threadgroup validates every compact float and transition, then emits a 64-byte generated-ABI status containing failure attribution, checked counts, runtime ABI, policy revision, task fingerprint, and a unique submission token. The CPU reads only this status before advancing a lease.
Fixed- and floating-base tasks share compiled semantic bindings, native joint/contact observations, reward, termination, reset, curriculum, and randomization.

TaskPack 17 compiles a topology-derived count of unique named scalar commands into immutable range, curriculum, and stable counter-RNG identity records. Actor, critic, and SignalIR sources resolve command identity to a stable slot once. Commands follow compact contact reductions in one native scalar-state arena whose resident and checkpoint capacities are compiler-derived. A five-command Metal fixture consumes its fifth command through SignalIR and recorder output; a variable fifth command is restored exactly after a rejected reset. Duplicate, unresolved, and invalid-range programs reject without replacing the last valid program. Vector-valued or correlated distributions and per-command schedules remain incomplete.

TaskPack 17 compiles named generalized-velocity-delta events into immutable target indices, curriculum endpoint ranges, and stable counter-RNG identities. A fixed-base two-event cohort executes deterministically on Metal, same-seed replay is exact, changed seeds separate, and TaskPack round-trip plus transactional invalid-program checks pass. G1 x/y perturbations are ordinary event records; the old floating-root push branch is deleted. Events currently share one cohort schedule; per-event schedules, scene-body wrench/state events, and other event operator kinds remain incomplete.

Compiled frames can target links in any articulation, static, kinematic, and dynamic scene bodies, or named model sites with compiler-composed site-local offsets. Explicit frame-to-frame operators publish reference-local position and tangent orientation across domains without overloading goals. World and moving-reference linear/angular velocity operators are materialized from accepted generalized and scene state once per control step, including the rotating-frame transport term; the same path supplies physically consistent support-slip and clearance metrics. Analytic world-axis linear/angular Jacobian components are available for articulated frame origins and named generalized-velocity coordinates. Fixed, episode-sampled, and two-pose trajectory SE(3) goals, generic scalar and cohort-reduction SignalIR, current SensorIR truth leaves, SensorIR actor/critic values, reset-correct pre-policy state, topology-sized named scalar commands, named generalized-velocity-delta events, generic reward reporting channels, three compact named recorders, and a SignalIR-driven scalar curriculum are implemented. Acceleration, arbitrary point queries, full Jacobian tensor outputs, multi-knot splines, vector or independently scheduled commands, independently scheduled or richer events, arbitrary recorder streams, richer curriculum operators, and three complete task families are not yet qualified.

TaskPack 17 compiles a topologically ordered scalar graph with semantic state/frame/current-SensorIR truth leaves, constants, arithmetic, min/max, absolute, square/root, safe division, clamp, exponential tracking/decay, atan2, comparisons, bounds gates, and contiguous source-cohort reductions. Resolved leaves include named scalar commands, heading-frame velocity, joint acceleration, action delta, compiled soft-limit violation, mechanical power, and desired support contact. The native order is accepted mechanics, SensorIR sample, dense sensor-source materialization, SignalIR, reward/termination/recorders, then actor/critic sensor-history publication. Scratch is topology-sized in the candidate-body arena and adds no persistent simulator tensor. General phase operator tables remain incomplete.

Every robot-shaped reward and termination opcode has been deleted. All nineteen bundled G1 reward terms compose generic SignalIR leaves, reductions, arithmetic, comparisons, and frame operators; each reward record contains only a resolved signal, channel, and weight. TaskPack 17 removes the joint-group wire section, duplicated compiled tables, task-complete DoF binding, anonymous locomotion command components, reward opcode enum, specialized shader switch, duplicate G1 metric/curriculum math, TaskPushProgram, and the floating-root push branch. Paired zero- and nonzero-action rollouts preserve physical outcomes, reward, recorder values, and reporting channels exactly across the command and event hard cuts.

A SignalIR reduction owns one contiguous truth-source cohort and compiles identity, absolute, or square transforms with sum, mean, minimum, or maximum. Direct mechanics sources are evaluated in place; SensorIR value and validity sources consume compiler-assigned dense current-sample slots. A fixed-base Metal fixture qualifies a two-source SensorIR sum-of-squares against the accepted post-step sensor view and rejects missing truth permission transactionally. The bundled G1 task uses eleven reductions inside a 92-node, 167-source generic reward, recorder, and curriculum graph and allocates zero sensor scratch.

Reward evaluation is a branchless lookup of a resolved SignalIR channel followed by an authored weight and generic reporting-channel accumulation. The bundled G1 task expresses command tracking, posture, acceleration, action rate, soft limits, power, contact gait intent, slip, forbidden contact, and foot clearance without a task-shaped native opcode, joint-group table, robot identity branch, or runtime mechanics-bound lookup. Compiler-resolved source parameters reject invalid soft factors, support groups, and ignored fields transactionally.

TaskPack compiles up to three unique named compact recorder bindings from SignalIR. The immutable session exposes ordered recorder identities while the 96-byte native transition carries only three generic values. A fixed-base runtime fixture proves recorder-to-reward-channel parity; G1 A/B rollouts preserve physical outcomes and metrics, and invalid identity, signal, or capacity changes fail transactionally. Arbitrary scheduled recorder streams remain incomplete.

A multi-level TaskPack binds its episode success metric to one resolved SignalIR node and compiles its evaluation window, threshold, survival fraction, and generic accepted-step phase period. The native global curriculum consumes only compact transition evidence. Missing success bindings reject transactionally. General command/event/curriculum operator tables and whole-session curriculum rollback remain incomplete.

TaskIR resolves a named articulated frame and generalized-velocity coordinate into a compiler-owned immutable point-query cohort. The existing analytic articulated operator publishes six world-axis spatial-Jacobian rows into a topology-sized native arena; TaskIR selects one linear or angular component without finite differences, string lookup, or another task kernel binding. Disconnected articulation coordinates evaluate to exact zero. The focused owner qualifies a scalar fixed-base column, TaskPack round trip, unresolved-coordinate rollback, accepted-state Jv parity, and the shared operator status contract. Arbitrary point authoring, scene-body generalized Jacobians, full tensor publication, and multi-DOF tangent-coordinate naming remain incomplete.

TaskPack compiles fixed, episode-sampled, and two-pose trajectory goals into one immutable table. Sampled world translation and local tangent orientation use stable per-goal counter keys; trajectories use accepted-step linear position and shortest-arc quaternion interpolation with clamp, loop, or ping-pong playback. Reset changes the episode key and failed transitions cannot advance derived goal time. Multi-knot path splines remain incomplete.

TaskIR resolves named SensorIR scalar values and validity bits, including fresh-but-invalid coherent dropout, enforces actor/critic permissions, fingerprints the exact sensor program, seeds histories transactionally on reset, advances them from accepted post-physics state, and republishes terminal policy/value views before inference.

Every native task step journals per-environment task state, including the shared event countdown, action delay, and the complete compiler-sized scalar arena containing contact reductions and named commands; reset steps additionally journal actor/critic/clean histories, previous velocity, sensor bias, and body/controller randomization. A rejected reset keeps its typed failure transition but restores hidden state, including an episode-resampled fifth command, and the next accepted physics, task, policy, sensor, and contact outputs match a no-failure reference branch byte-for-byte. Global curriculum scheduling is not included.
Native deformation, contact evidence, wrench summaries, history, and device-buffer access.

Native scalar-joint state, parent-frame pose, world-space frame-twist, six-axis IMU, six-axis contact-wrench, and five-channel contact-state sensors use topology-derived persistent buffers, reset-only seeding, accepted-state advancement, deterministic nanosecond phase accumulation, whole-sample latency history, and compact value/age/validity publication. Joint state reads accepted q/v directly and a joint-only plan omits kinematics. Twist linear velocity is evaluated at the authored sensor origin. Force-torque and contact-state consume final-microstep NumiSolver impulses; semantic contact filters are immutable compiled tables. The owner covers articulated and rigid kinematic parents, exact 50 Hz and non-divisor 30 Hz schedules, reset-cleared contact signals, and task-independent execution.

A generic body-attached IMU publishes sensor-local specific force followed by sensor-local angular velocity. Specific force differentiates accepted sensor-origin world velocity over the exact scheduled interval and subtracts world gravity; previous point velocity and timestamp are persistent transactionally journaled SensorIR state. The owner checks a rotated kinematic parent against an analytic acceleration/gravity/gyro result and includes IMU state in rejected-reset branch equivalence.

An asset-owned joint-state sensor resolves one authored scalar revolute, prismatic, or continuous joint into stable joint and q/v indices and publishes accepted position and velocity through the common native schedule. Joint-only free-motion execution omits kinematics pipelines. The owner checks exact q/v publication, TaskIR binding, transactional unresolved-name rejection, and WorldPack semantic-target persistence. Fixed and multi-DOF targets are explicitly rejected until their tangent-coordinate observation contract lands.

Only environments requesting reset journal their SensorIR schedule state, corruption episode identity, complete latency ring, compact output, and metadata in private topology-sized buffers. A rejected world or contact transaction restores the journal byte-for-byte, keeps the resident token valid, and permits a following submission; successful and ordinary non-reset steps perform no checkpoint copy.

Six-axis SensorIR force-torque sums committed non-generalized contact impulses on the parent body, divides by the final accepted physics-microstep duration, shifts the moment to the authored sensor origin, and expresses force and torque in sensor-local axes. All six channels match TaskIR's independent contact-group reduction and reset clears the view. Control-window integration and joint-transmission load-cell semantics remain incomplete.

A generic body-attached contact-state sensor publishes active state, accepted contact-block count, summed normal force, resultant tangential force, and maximum penetration from committed NumiSolver constraints. Optional semantic counterpart-body filters compile into a canonical immutable index table. The focused owner mirrors all five reductions analytically, proves a negative filter remains zero, rejects an unresolved filter transactionally, round-trips the semantic filter through WorldPack, binds the result into TaskIR, and includes its state in reset rollback.

Native scalar SensorIR publication applies episode-static Gaussian bias, per-acquired-sample Gaussian value noise, and coherent whole-sensor dropout from a stateless counter key containing session seed, environment, episode, stable sensor ID, sample, channel, and purpose. Pose orientation noise is a normalized tangent-space rotation; contact-state discrete channels remain exact. The owner checks host-mirrored twist and pose values, exact replay, seed separation, episode reset, explicit dropped validity through TaskIR, WorldPack persistence, and rejected-reset rollback. Presentation and tactile corruption remain in their current native owners until schedule unification.

WorldPack joint-state, actuator-state, frame-state, frame-twist, IMU, force-torque, contact-state, image, and tactile declarations compile transactionally into one generated-ABI descriptor table. Spatial sensors may bind named model sites, which compile into the same body-frame records. Scalar-joint and actuator state, frame pose/twist, IMU, force-torque, and semantically filtered contact-state sensors execute in the session-owned scheduler with reset-failure journals, native counter-based corruption, and TaskIR bindings; presentation and tactile still use their existing native owners, while scheduled recorder-stream routing, ray, and LiDAR operators remain incomplete.

Fingerprint-bound normalization, dense actor/critic layers, Gaussian behavior policy, and native inference. Each dense output is reduced cooperatively in FP32 by one SIMDgroup, up to eight outputs share a threadgroup, and the owner compares nonzero rollout outputs with a host dot-product reference. SIMDgroup matrix tiles and reduced-precision storage remain unqualified.

A stable topology fingerprint locks the compiled policy shape. Changed parameters require a monotonic revision, upload into the inactive one of two private Metal banks, and become active only at a native submission boundary. The task owner proves A-to-B-to-A reuse; the Swift integration rejects stale and topology-changing updates transactionally. Direct no-copy MLX-to-bank blits remain incomplete.
Convolution, recurrence, and attention are not production PolicyIR operators.
Forward Jacobians exist, but no production tape, backward kernels, implicit adjoint, or validity-mask API exists.
Authored Visual Presentation V3 path; collision geometry is not a visual fallback.
